items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And Mr. Frank Schiff was the Lafayette Theater there... He was. First violinist. And when his retirement came he had some savings, so he bought this Hotcha Club... he renamed the place in honor of the tap dancers, the Hoofer's Club.

ctx.x: But tell me a little bit about the guy that owned the Hoofer's Club and the way it was laid out. There was a front room and there was a back room for the dancers. What was in the front room?

Oh, yes. That was Mr. Dudley, his name was. John Dudley, I think. He used to be a first violinist. And Mr. Frank Schiff was the Lafayette Theater there. Until he reached his retirement, which was -- they were in the house orchestra, see? He was. First violinist. And when his retirement came he had some savings, so he bought this Hotcha Club, it used to be, an ex-nightclub. And by the tap dancers coming

down there, he used to adopt these tap dancers, the ones that were allowed to get into the Hoofer's Club fraternity. And he renamed the place in honor of the tap dancers, the Hoofer's Club. It really was a recreation place, you know, for people to come and relax and have lunches and dinners and so on, you know. They had a gorgeous kitchen there. See, it was a circular kitchen, so you had number one chef, number two chef, and so on, on down the road, see? And they fixed everything. Whatever you wanted, any way in…
